cohort: The study participants were 1,226 female Turkish university students aged 26.53 ± 10.082.
finding: The study found that the prevalence of urinary incontinence was 19.5%, gas incontinence was 29.1%, stool incontinence was 0.5%, and combined stool and gas incontinence was 1.6% among the participants.
cross-section timing: At a single point in time via an internet-based questionnaire.
